facts.fact: Best resources: gRPC core concepts, proto3 guide, Google AIPs, Stripe API reference and idempotency post, Fowler on Richardson, gRPC performance and deadlines guides, GraphQL learn
facts.verdict: verified (all URLs answer 200 on 2026-10-05)
facts.where: Further reading; Stripe idempotency post left to Building a backend API and HTTP, which own idempotency keys

facts.fact: REST is an architectural style from Fielding's 2000 dissertation, chapter 5
facts.verdict: verified

facts.fact: Constraints: resources, representations, uniform interface (GET safe and cacheable, PUT/DELETE idempotent, POST neither), statelessness, cacheability and layered system, HATEOAS least followed
facts.verdict: verified (Fielding ch5; RFC 9110 method properties)

facts.fact: REST as practised is resource-oriented HTTP+JSON; 'HTTP API' is the honest name
facts.verdict: kept

facts.fact: Richardson levels 0 to 3; L2 is where most stop
facts.verdict: verified (Fowler, 18 March 2010)

facts.fact: :verb custom methods, AIP-136, POST /models/m1:deploy
facts.verdict: verified; example replaced by AIP-136's own (:archive)

facts.fact: Cursor pagination over offset, opaque cursor plus has_more, paginate from day one
facts.verdict: owned by Building a backend API (measured there on Postgres)

facts.fact: Idempotency-Key header pattern
facts.verdict: owned by HTTP (s9) and Building a backend API; the IETF draft expired (root atlas correction 16)

facts.fact: Versioning: URL major versions, Stripe date pinning, additive changes non-breaking, deprecation policy; anthropic-version is date-based
facts.verdict: owned by Building a backend API; anthropic-version kept

facts.fact: RFC 9457 problem+json error shape
facts.verdict: verified (atlas)

facts.fact: Long-running operations: 202 + operation resource or webhook; AIP-151; SageMaker async and LLM batch APIs are this
facts.verdict: corrected in detail: AIP-151 returns an Operation object (202 is plain HTTP's way); Anthropic Message Batches verified as the example; SageMaker not re-verified, dropped

facts.fact: gRPC: services and messages in protobuf, codegen for about a dozen languages, binary wire format with field numbers and varints, unknown fields ignored
facts.verdict: verified and measured (49 vs 117 bytes; unknown fields round-trip byte-identical)

facts.fact: Never reuse or renumber field numbers; use reserved
facts.verdict: verified and measured (reuse silently misreads)

facts.fact: Four streaming modes; all ride HTTP/2 streams on one connection
facts.verdict: verified (PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md); server streaming recorded frame by frame
facts.where: Reading s4, One gRPC call tab

facts.fact: Deadlines propagate across hops; abort work past the deadline; prevents wasted GPU time
facts.verdict: verified and measured (four runs)

facts.fact: Status codes UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, INVALID_ARGUMENT; retry policy per code in service config
facts.verdict: verified; all 17 codes tabled, 10 failures measured

facts.fact: Only UNAVAILABLE-class errors are safely retryable by default
facts.verdict: corrected: no application-level retry by default, only transparent retries; no fixed list (statuscodes.md)

facts.fact: L4 load balancer pins a gRPC channel to one backend; need L7 (Envoy, ALB gRPC, mesh) or client-side LB (xDS, round_robin); number-one production surprise
facts.verdict: verified and measured (30/0/0 vs 10/10/10; scale-up timelines); added: default pick_first also pins

facts.fact: Interceptors, TLS/mTLS native, grpc-web/Connect for browsers, server reflection, health checking
facts.verdict: verified (gRPC-Web spec, Connect protocol, health and reflection recorded); interceptors in s4; mTLS owned by TLS and Auth pages

facts.fact: When to use gRPC and when not
facts.verdict: kept

facts.fact: tRPC: no relation to gRPC, TypeScript end-to-end types, no codegen, HTTP/JSON wire, batching, subscriptions over SSE/WS, compile-time contract only
facts.verdict: verified (tRPC README, v11.19.0)

facts.fact: tRPC vs gRPC table
facts.verdict: kept, one cell reworded

facts.fact: GraphQL: client-specified queries, one endpoint, resolvers; costs: caching hard, N+1, query cost limits, schema work; GitHub's public API
facts.verdict: verified and measured (N+1 21 vs 2, 141 vs 4; static cost); added GitHub limits, GraphQL-over-HTTP status codes, RFC 10008 QUERY

facts.fact: gRPC is the internal lingua franca; Triton HTTP and gRPC (KServe v2), gRPC preferred for tensors and streaming
facts.verdict: verified (Triton docs: both protocols; Triton actually recommends unary calls and streams only for sequences)

facts.fact: Ray/Ray Serve internals, TF Serving, vector DBs (Qdrant, Milvus), OTLP speak gRPC
facts.verdict: partly verified: Ray Serve gRPC proxy, TF Serving 8500, Qdrant, OTLP 4317 confirmed; Ray internals and Milvus not confirmed today, not carried

facts.fact: Tensor payloads in protobuf beat base64-in-JSON by a wide margin
facts.verdict: corrected by measurement: about 4/3 in size against base64-in-JSON, about 5x against a JSON number list

facts.fact: REST + SSE is the external face of LLM APIs
facts.verdict: verified (root running request)

facts.fact: Mixed pattern: public REST facade, gRPC behind the gateway, transcoding; vLLM and SGLang serve OpenAI-compatible REST
facts.verdict: verified and extended: vLLM v0.31.0 --grpc mode, SGLang gRPC server entry point

facts.fact: AWS: SageMaker endpoints HTTPS/JSON; API Gateway REST and WebSocket but not gRPC; ALB does gRPC; Lambda does not fit gRPC
facts.verdict: ALB verified (2020-10-29 announcement); the rest unconfirmed today, not carried
